like or be attracted to something or someone; {laibu ngaina mi} is a lover of books
<ngai>, listen, said twice for continued action: keep on listening
after <lung>, heart: {lung ngaingai} is <lungngai>, ponder, with its second part said twice, keep turning a matter over in the heart, not listening with the ears
politics, the affairs of state and of parties; {Ngaingngaanzee party} is a political party; one writer spells the Burmese word this way and with a capital

terms: want to listen/be willing to listen
definition: <ngai>, listen, with <nuam>, want
<ngai>, listen or heed, with the causative <sak>: make someone or something obey
<ngai>, listen, with <sim>, secretly: listen in on what others are saying
another spelling of <ngaihsun>, think; {bangci na ngaisun hiam} is what do you think

terms: those who listen/those who heed/those who welcome
definition: <ngai>, listen or heed, with plural <te>: the ones who listen to someone; also of those who welcome a person

terms: those who miss/those who love/loved ones
definition: <ngai.2>, miss or be fond of, with plural {-te}: the people who love someone and feel his absence, in the condolence formula {a it a ngaite}, those who love and miss him; not those who listen

terms: fall in love at once/take to at once
definition: <ngai>, love, <thei>, can, and <pah>, at once, written as one word: come to love someone straight away, as at first sight

terms: love more/hold dearer/be more attached to
definition: <ngai>, here love or long for, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: love someone or something more
<ngai>, listen, with <zo>, carry through: do what one was told; {thu ngaizo} is obey a word
wait for someone or something, or stay awake and keep watch
<ngak>, wait for, and the linking <a> written as one word: while waiting for, depending on; {lupna ngaka} is confined to bed
<ngak>, wait, and <bawl> written as one word: wait on purpose for something to happen or to pass
<ngak>, wait, and <cip>, firmly, written as one word: wait without leaving, or stay on guard at a place
<ngak>, wait, and <ding>, will, written as one word: will wait, or having to wait
<ngak>, wait, with the linking suffix <in>: waiting, while waiting; often followed by <om>, be
staying in one place without leaving it, said of a sick person or of one who minds the house: {lupna ngakin om} is be bedridden and {inn ngakin om} is stay at home keeping the house
<ngak>, wait, and <kawm>, while, written as one word, usually followed by <in>: while waiting for something
<ngak>, wait, with <kawm>, while, and the linking suffix <in>: while waiting for something
<ngak>, wait, with <kawm>, while, and <un>, the linking suffix for more than one person: while you wait
<ngak>, wait or watch, with <khawm>, together
<ngak>, lay or rest upon, with <khit>, finish: have laid on, said of laying hands on someone; {ngakkhit ciangin} is after laying on
<ngak> and <kul> written as one word: it is necessary to wait
<ngak>, wait, and <kulding>, will have to, written as one word
wait for or want something with impatience, be eager for it; {an ngaklah} is be greedy for food
<ngaklah>, wait eagerly, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: something one looks forward to or is eager to see
<ngaklah>, long for, with the linking suffix <in>: longing, while longing
<ngaklah>, wait eagerly, with the noun ending {-na}: eager or impatient waiting for something, also the complaint of one who is tired of waiting
<ngak> wait, with <lai> still, any longer
<ngak>, wait, with <laitak>, at the very time, written as one word: at present still waiting; after <ki>, is now being awaited
punctuation mark: the semicolon, a longer stop than <husanna>, the comma, and shorter than <ngakna>, the colon
the punctuation mark colon, written in place of a comma before quoted words when {a ci hi}, he said, is left out, as after the name of the speaker in a dialogue
<ngak>, wait, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<ngak>, rest or lay upon, with the noun suffix <na>: the thing on which something rests, as the stand of a basin; {khe ngakna} is a footstool
<ngak>, wait, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of waiting or the place where one waits, as {Bus ngakna}, a bus stop; not {ngakna} a stand on which a thing rests
punctuation mark, the waiting place, from <ngak>, wait: the colon
plural of <ngakna>: things on which something rests; {ban ngaknate} are armrests, and the {ngaknate} of a basin are its stand
plural of <ngakna> in the sense of waiting: the times one waits patiently, perseverance
<ngak>, wait, doubled to show that the waiting goes on
after a verb of speaking such as <kici> or <cih>, with no thought of waiting: the thing is said or done again and again, as a habit
<ngak> wait, said twice for continued action, with the noun suffix <na> and <in> marking the cause: because of waiting and waiting

terms: wait a long time/wait and wait
definition: <ngak>, wait, with the descriptive word <ngeungau>: keep waiting long and wearily
<ngak>, rest upon, with the causative <sak>: lay or place on; {khut ngaksak} is lay a hand on a person
<ngak> in its meaning wait, with the causative <sak>: make someone wait or keep someone waiting, as passengers for a bus or applicants for an office; not lay a hand on
<ngaksak>, lay on, with the linking suffix <in>; {lupna ngaksakin} is laying someone on a bed
those on whom something has been laid, here the hands, from <ngak> lay upon, <sa> already and plural <te>
<ngak>, wait, with plural <te>: people who wait for someone or put their hope in him
<ngak> in its meaning keep watch over a place, with plural <te>: the people who mind a place, as in {sumbuk ngakte} shop attendants and {inn ngakte} those who stay to mind the house
<ngak>, wait, with <zaw>, rather: wait instead of doing something else
<ngak>, wait, and <zawh>, finish or be able, written as one word; the form of <ngakzo> used before <ding>, <hangin> and <ciangin>: be able to wait, or have waited a length of time
<ngakzo>, be able to wait, with the noun suffix <na>: the ability to wait, patience

terms: be able to wait/manage to wait/wait through
definition: <ngak> wait, keep watch, with <zo>, be able, manage to
<ngakzo> and <lo> written as one word: not manage to wait

terms: those who wait/those who can wait
definition: <ngakzo>, be able to wait, with the plural {-te}: those who manage to wait, as in the saying that good things come to those who wait
a wild pig that lives in the forest
placed after <kei>, not, and before <leh>, if, to stress the condition: {kei ngal leh} is unless, if indeed not
the second half of the pair <tha leh ngal>, strength and effort: the bodily work a person gives, named beside money and skill; not the animal
after <lo> or <loh>, not, as in {cih loh ngal} and {cih ding lo ngal}: apart from that, followed by a statement that there is nothing else or that all the rest is different
a wild pig that lives in the forest; the same word as <ngal>, written with a capital in one text
<ngal>, strength, with <hat>, strong: strong and full of vigour, the opposite of <zawngkhal>, weak
a wild boar that goes about alone, from <ngal>, wild boar, and <khaat>, single; {ngalkhaat bang} is like a lone boar, said of one who acts alone and does not join with others
a kind of wild bee or hornet, <khuai>, that moves its nest from place to place; the exact kind is not settled
a brave man who fights for his people, a word of songs and of praise; {Zomi ngalliam} is a hero of the Zomi
<nga> and <lo> written as one word: not turned toward something; {ki ngalo} is not depend on
the jointed upper leg above the foot that an insect such as a locust uses for hopping

<ngal>, wild boar, with <tang>: a full-grown boar, bigger game than a deer; known from the saying {sakhi man lo ngaltang tum}, not having caught a deer one aims for a boar, said of reaching for the greater thing before having the lesser
Saying: the tusk of a <ngaltang>, a big boar, once grown out never goes back in; a man does not take back a word he has spoken
a kind of wasp or hornet that has grubs and no honey, named beside <ngaltun> and <tuunpi>; its nest is taken at the <Khuado> festival and addressed in the song of the <khuai>
armour worn on the lower legs, in the verse made of bronze
a kind of wild bee or wasp, named together with <ngalthen> and <khuaithuum>; its nest was looked at for omens at the Khuado festival; the exact kind is not determined
plural with <te>: small animals of little strength that make their home among the rocks
have the courage to do something; placed after the main verb, and very often used with <kei> or <lo>, not dare
<ngam>, dare, and <ding> written as one word after a verb: to dare to do it, will dare to do it
<ngam>, dare, with the linking suffix <in>; follows the verb that names what is dared, as in {nuntakna pia ngamin}, risking life
<ngam>, dare, and <kei>, not, written as one word and placed after the main verb
<ngam>, dare, with <lah>, fail to: not have the courage to do something, hold back from it
<ngam>, dare, and <lel>, just, written as one word after a verb: do it boldly and without hesitation
<ngam>, dare, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not dare to do it
<ngam> and <loh> written as one word after a verb: that one does not dare to do, as in {gen ngamloh}, that one dare not say
<ngam>, dare, with <lohna> written as one word after a verb: the fact of not daring to do it; {pai ngamlohna mun} is a place where one dare not go
<ngamlo>, dare not, with the plural <te> after a verb: the people who do not dare to do it
<ngam>, dare, and <mawk> written as one word, after a verb: do a bold or shocking thing without fear or shame, as in broad daylight
<ngam>, dare, with the noun suffix <na>: being bold enough to do something; placed after the verb, as in {gen ngamna}, daring to speak
<ngamna>, daring, with plural <te>; {mawh gamtat ngamnate} is their daring to act sinfully
<ngam>, dare, with <pa>, the male one: the one who dares to do something
<ngam>, dare, and the particle <ta>, now or already, written as one word after a verb: now dare to, have come to dare
<ngam>, dare, with plural <te>: the ones who dared to do something; {ngawng a dawh ngamte} are those who risked their necks
<ngam>, dare, with <zaw>, more or rather; {sum ngamzaw} is be willing rather to lose
<nga>, five, with <na>, which makes an ordinal number: fifth; {sawm-le-ngana} is fifteenth
<nga>, fish, with <neu>, small
placed after a verb of pain, describing a continual throbbing ache; {tum ngangngang} is ache without stopping
<nga> and <ni> written as one word: the fifth day; {Ni ngani}, the fifth day of the week, is the Bible name of Thursday in the book's table
have the courage or the strength to do something; {na ngap nak leh} is if you dare, {ka ngap kei} is I am not up to it
cross water on foot, as at a ford; {ka ngap zo kei hi}, I could not get across
beach and resort on the coast of Rakhine State in Myanmar, near Thandwe
<nga>, fish, with <pi>, big: the great fish that swallowed Jonah
Burmese fermented paste of fish or shrimp, with a strong smell, eaten as a relish
second part of the pair {utkeng ngapkeng}, from <ut>, want, and <ngap>, dare: doing just what one likes and dares, without regard for what is due

terms: not dare/cannot bear to/not be up to
definition: <ngap>, dare or be up to, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not have the heart or the strength to do it
<ngap> and <loh> written as one word: not having the strength or heart for something; {ngaploh hun} is a time when one is not up to it
<ngap>, dare, doubled: keep daring, do something boldly and without holding back
<ngap> ford, with <tan>, cut across: go through water on foot; with <sak>, lead someone through
<ngaptan> wade through, with <sak>, cause to: take someone across water on foot

terms: be able to wade across/be able to ford
definition: <ngap>, wade across, with <zo>, be able
a fish, as a living creature and as food; {ngasa bengte} are fishermen
capitalised form of <ngasa> fish, in the name {Ngasa Kongpi}, the Fish Gate of Jerusalem
<nga>, face or be turned toward, with the causative <sak>: make a thing face a direction; of hands, lay them on someone
<ngasa>, fish, with <lip>, scale
catching fish with a hook; {ngasiahna sikkawi} is a fish hook
put a carried thing down, with <suk>, downward: lower a jar or a sack to the ground
turn a part of the body toward something; {bil ngat} is incline the ear, pay attention, {mai ngat} is set the face toward, and {nung ngat} is turn the back on
stream followed and crossed on the way from <Zangpitam> to <Ciimnuai>
<nga>, five, with the plural <te>: the five things of a set that is named before it, as in {Solas ngate}, the five Solas, and after {sawm le} the fifteen; not fish
<ngat>, turn toward, with the linking ending <in>: with the face or ear turned toward something while another action follows
after the name of a weapon, as in {temta ngatin}, with a knife pointed at someone to threaten him while another action follows; not the face or ear turned toward something
<ngat>, face or turn toward, with the noun suffix <na>; the side or direction toward which a thing is turned
with <to>, upward, and <in>, linking to the next verb: lifting a load up onto the shoulder
<ngat>, face, with the causative <sak>: make something face a certain way
strictly, without exception: <ngat> with <takin>, which makes an adverb; said of a law that must be strictly obeyed
a long-tailed kind of monkey; the proverb {zawng nek ngau in thuak lawh} says that the langur suffers for what the monkey ate
paired with <zawn>, poor, as {zawn leh ngau}: poor and destitute
the state of having nothing; nearly always said together with <zawnna>, poverty, as {zawnna ngauna}, poverty and want
placed after a verb of feeling, asking or saying: with deep and lasting feeling, earnestly and again and again, as in {lunggulh ngaungau}, long for keenly, and {kap ngaungau}, keep whining
<nga>, five, with <vei>, times
<ngavei>, five times, written with a capital at the start of a sentence
<ngavei>, five times, with the ordinal suffix <na>: the fifth time
written twice, {ngaw ngaw} or {ngaw-ngaw}: at last, only then, after a wait or several attempts
probably a spelling of <ngawng>, neck; {a ngawg kuaitan} is break its neck
lay the guilt for something on someone; {sihna sisan ngawh} is hold someone accountable for a death
placed before or after a verb, harshly or in anger; {ngawh dawn} is answer harshly
<ngawh>, accuse, with <bawl>, do: lay the blame on someone, often for something not proved
<ngawh>, accuse, with <bawlna>, doing, written as one word: the act of accusing someone, or the accusation made
<ngawh>, harshly, with <dawn>, answer: give someone a harsh answer
<ngawh>, blame, with the linking suffix <in>: blaming; {Topa ngawhin heh} is be angry and put the blame on the Lord
a claim that someone has done wrong; {ngawhna nial} is deny an accusation and {ngawhna tuak} is be accused
plural of <ngawhna>: the charges laid against someone
<ngawh>, in anger, with <piak>, give: give something in anger
a barrier or trap set in a stream to catch fish
go without something; {an ngawl} is go without food, fast
after <an>, food: keep someone wholly without food, from <ngawl>, go without, and <cip>, completely
<ngawl>, go without, with the linking suffix <in>; {an ngawlin} is going without food, fasting
<ngawl>, go without, and the causing <sak> written as one word: make someone go without something; {an ngawlsak} is leave without food, starve, and of a habit, make someone give it up
word of emphasis placed after a verb or after <kei>, stressing that something is surely so or surely not so; {na ngawn} is another way of writing <nangawn>, even
the neck of a person or animal; {ngawng tan} is behead, and {puan ngawng} is the collar of a garment
<ngawng>, neck, and <tansak>, have cut off: behead a person; the person stands before it, often with <a>, his or her
<ngawng>, neck, with the place marker <ah>: on or around the neck, said of a yoke, a chain or a millstone
word of emphasis placed after a time or a verb: only at that point, at long last, not before
<ngawng>, neck, with the marker <in>: by the neck; {ngawngin man} is seize by the neck
<ngawng>, neck, with <kawi>, embrace, and the linking suffix <in>: putting the arms around the neck of someone
<ngawng>, neck, with <sa>, meat: the meat of the neck of a slaughtered animal
<ngawng>, neck, and <sau>, long, written as one word: with a long neck; {sa ngawngsau} is a giraffe and {khedap ngawngsau} a boot
<ngawng>, neck, and <tan>, cut off, written as one word: cut off the head, behead
<ngawngtan>, behead, and <sak> written as one word: cut off the head of someone, or have someone beheaded
{ngawngzang}, the neck or nape, with the place marker <ah>: on the neck, said of a yoke or load
<ngawn> and <in> written as one word after <na> or {te na}: the second part of {na ngawn in}, the same as <nangawn>, even
<ngawn> and <zong>, also, written as one word, for {nangawn zong} with its first part written apart: even that, even in that case
placed after a verb to show that the action is done heavily, thoroughly or all over; close in use to <gawp>
soft and very young; said of infants, young animals and new grass, and in {a ngeek dikdek} of a delicate woman
<ngeek>, tender, with <bawl>, treat: handle someone gently and with great care, pamper
placed after a verb for an action done with force and kept up without a break, as beating, walking on or enduring
<ngeek>, tender, with the plural ending <te>, of what is very young and soft; {ta ngeekte} is newborn babies and {lopa ngeekte} is tender grass
another spelling of <ngen>, a net for catching fish
expressive word placed after a verb of going or lining up, as <kigual>: in a long line, many following one after another
placed after a verb: have ever done or been so; with <kei> or <lo> it means never
<ngei>, ever, and <nailoh>, not yet: placed after a verb and before the noun it describes or before <hangin>, never yet done until now, as {muh ngei nailoh}, never seen before
<ngei>, ever, and <nawn>, any more: placed after a verb and followed by a negative such as <lo> or <kei>, never again
<ngei>, before, with the place marker <ah>; {omna ngeiah} is at the place where one was before
<ngei> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will ever do or happen, will at some time; with <lo> or <kei>, will never
<ngei> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a sentence: it has happened before, has once done so
<ngei>, ever, and the question word <hiam>, written as one word after a verb: has it ever been so, whether one has ever done it
expressive word after <ot> shout, describing loud ringing shouting
<ngei>, ever, with <kei>, not, placed after a verb: will never, or may it never, be so
<ngei> and <khat> written as one word after a verb or a noun: one who has done or been so before, a former one
<ngei>, ever, and <khin>, already, written as one word after a verb: the thing has already happened or been done before now
<ngei> and <khinsa> written as one word after a verb: the thing has already happened once before now
<ngei> and <khollo> written as one word after a verb: has hardly ever happened or been so
<ngei>, ever, with <lo>, not, placed after a verb: has never done or has never been so
form of <ngeilo>, never, used inside a dependent clause, as before <hangin>, although, or before a noun
<ngeiloh>, never, with the suffix <na> joining it to a following noun: {a kizak ngeilohna mun} is a place where it has never been heard
<ngeiloh>, never, and the plural <te> written as one word, after a verb: the things or people that one has never seen, heard or known
<ngeilo>, never, with the plural <te>, after a verb: those who never do it, those who have never done so
<ngei>, have ever, and <mawk>, unexpectedly, written as one word after a verb: such a thing has in fact happened before
the customary way of doing things, handed down from the ancestors; {biakna ngeina} is a fixed rule of worship

<ngeina>, custom, and <bangmah>, here <bang> and <mah>, just like, not the word for nothing: just as is the custom or practice; followed by <in> and placed after the word or clause that says whose practice or what practice
<ngeina>, custom, and <dante>, ways: the customs and practices of a people, and in the papers of an organisation its bylaws, named beside <thukhunpi>, the constitution
<ngeina>, custom, with <la>, song: a song that belongs to the customs handed down from the forefathers
<ngeina>, custom, and <van>, here goods or things and not heaven: the articles that belong to a tradition, such as dress, tools and instruments shown at a cultural event
<ngei>, ever, and <nai>, yet, written as one word after a verb; with a negative it means never yet
<ngei> ever and <nailo> not yet written as one word after a verb: has never yet done or been so
<ngeina>, tradition, and <laam>, dance, written as one word: a dance of the tradition of a people, shown at a festival
<ngeina>, custom, with the plural <te>: the customs of a people, or the rules laid down for worship
<ngeina>, custom, with <zah>, amount: as much as is usual; {ngeinazah sangin} is more than usual
expressive word placed after a verb, showing that the action goes on in a noisy stir or commotion, often by many people at once
<ngeingai> with the noun ending <na>, placed after a verb: the doing of something in a noisy stir by many people together, as fighting in a brawl or working busily side by side
placed after a verb or phrase to stress that it really is so or will surely be so; with <kei>, certainly not
<ngei> said twice, with <sa>, already: what has been done or heard time and again before
<ngei> said twice, with the plural <te>: things that happen again and again; {mite tuah ngeingeite} is what people commonly meet with
<ngei>, have done or been before, with <pa>, the male one; after a verb or descriptive word, the man who did so or was so before, as in {a mittaw ngeipa}, the man who had been blind
placed after a verb or noun for what has been, or was done, before; from <ngei>, ever, and <sa>, already
<ngeisa>, former, with the plural <te>; {ka pianzia ngeisate} is my former way of life
<ngei> and the emphatic <se> written as one word, before a negative: {ngeise lo} is never at all, not even once
the rhododendron tree and its flower, {ngeisok kung} and {ngeisok paak}; also found in place names
<ngei> with the plural <te> after a verb: the things one is used to doing, or the ones who have done so before; {gamtat ngeite} is the accustomed ways
<ngei> with <teng>, all, after a verb: all that one usually does or did before

terms: the usual amount/as much as before
definition: <ngei> with <zah>, amount, after a verb: the amount one used to do or have
<ngei> with <zel>, habitually; {hih ngeizel bangin} is according to what is customarily done
<ngei> with <zo>, placed after a verb to say that something was so or was done in the past
small and soft like a newborn; {a no ngek} is a tender young one, and {a ngek pen} is the least or smallest
<ngek>, tender, with <bawl>, make: treat someone very gently, as one treats a small child, and so also spoil
<ngek>, tender, with the suffix <in>: in a delicate way
<ngek>, tender, with <lai>, still: still tiny; {no ngeklai} is young that are still suckling

terms: on and on/without a break/again and again
definition: expressive word placed after a verb: the action goes on hard and without a break, or comes again and again one after another, as in {kizom ngekngek}, keep on coming, and {kikap ngekngek}, keep on shooting at each other
<ngek>, tiny, with <pen>, most: the smallest or least of all
<ngek>, tiny, with <sih>, die: die as an infant
soft and refined, not used to hardship; said of a man or woman brought up in comfort
placed after a verb for emphasis; {pia ngel ding} is would certainly have given
<ngel>, surely, and <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb, often after <kha>: it must surely be so, a confident guess of the writer
placed after <kun>, bow, describing heads hanging low
placed after a verb or describing word for emphasis: really and truly so, actually doing it
<ngel>, certainly, with the suffix <in>; {thei kisa ngelin} is as though knowing for certain
what is planned or arranged in the mind; {ngaihsutna ngelna} is thoughts and plans
<ngel> said twice, placed after a verb; with <ding> it says that something must surely be so
<ngelngel>, surely, and <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb: it must surely be so
ask someone to give something; the form <nget> is used in dependent clauses
pray, in the phrase {thu ngen}, literally ask a matter; {Topa tungah thu ngen} is pray to the Lord
a net for catching fish, birds or animals; {ngen paai} is cast a net

terms: to ask for/will ask for/will request
definition: <ngen>, ask for, and <ding>, will, written as one word; {huhna ngending in} is in order to ask for help
big in size, given by the book as the same as <gol>, in a sentence about an elephant
<ngen> said twice: go on asking; {thu ngengen} is keep on praying
expressive word after a verb for something very great and overwhelming, as smoke billowing up or thunder roaring
<ngen>, ask for, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: asks for, asked for; {huhna ngenhi} is asked for help
<ngen>, ask, with the linking suffix <in>; {thu ngenin} is praying
<ngen> and <kawikawi> written as one word: ask for something here and there, from one place or person after another
<ngen>, pray, with <khawm>, together; {thu ngenkhawm} is pray together
<ngen>, pray or ask, with <kik>, again
<ngen>, ask, with <kik> in the sense of back and not of again: ask for the return of what one gave, deposited or had taken away, such as money or land
<ngen> and <lo> written as one word: not ask for; {man ngenlo in} is without asking payment, free of charge
<ngen>, ask for, and <loin>, without, written as one word: without asking for something; <man ngenloin> is free of charge
<ngen> and <masa> written as one word: ask for a thing first, before anything else
<ngen> said twice: ask or pray again and again; {thu ngenngen} is keep praying
<ngenngen>, keep praying, with the suffix <in>: by praying again and again
<ngenngen>, keep asking, with <kha>, happen to: went on asking, in the verse to no purpose
village in Tedim Township, Chin State
<ngen>, ask, with <pa> marking a man: the man who asks; {khutdawh ngenpa} is a beggar
<ngen>, ask, with <pah>, straightaway: ask directly
<ngen>, net, with <pi>, big: a large net dragged through the water
<ngen>, ask, with <sak>, cause or allow: send someone to ask, or let someone ask
<ngen>, ask for, with <ta>, now or already, written as one word: has asked for, now asks for
placed after a list of nouns or qualities: these and nothing else, all of that kind
<ngen>, ask, with the plural <te>: the people who ask or pray; {hong ngente} is those who ask you
<ngen>, a net, with the plural <te>
